text: SUPPLY CHAIN PROCUREMENT AND INVENTORY POLICY Policy ID: SCP-001 | Version: 1.0 | Effective Date: 01 September 2026 1. Purpose This policy defines the standard rules for procurement, supplier selection, inventory replenishment, emergency purchasing, and logistics decisions. The objective is to maintain product availability while controlling procurement, holding, and transportation costs. 2. Scope This policy applies to all procurement and inventory activities involving company products, warehouses, approved suppliers, purchase orders, and transportation partners. 3. Reorder Point A purchase order should normally be initiated when available inventory reaches or falls below the calculated Reorder Point (ROP). ROP = Expected Demand During Lead Time + Safety Stock The Inventory Management System shall use current demand forecasts and approved lead-time data when calculating ROP. 4. Safety Stock Safety stock should be maintained for products with demand or lead-time uncertainty. The target safety stock may be adjusted according to the required service level, historical demand variability, and supplier reliability. Critical products should receive higher protection against stockout risk. 5. Economic Order Quantity (EOQ) EOQ may be used to determine an economically appropriate order quantity when demand, ordering cost, and holding cost are sufficiently stable. EOQ = sqrt((2 × Annual Demand × Ordering Cost) / Annual Holding Cost per Unit) EOQ is a decision-support quantity and may be adjusted when supplier minimum order quantities, warehouse capacity, shelf life, or contractual restrictions apply. 6. Supplier Selection Suppliers should be evaluated using the following factors: - Unit procurement cost - Lead time - Historical delivery reliability - Product quality - Available capacity - Minimum order quantity - Contractual terms A low purchase price alone should not determine supplier selection. For critical products, reliability and lead time must also be considered. 7. Supplier Reliability A supplier with historical on-time delivery below 90% should be classified as requiring review. Suppliers with on-time delivery below 80% require a risk review before being selected for critical-product orders, unless an authorized exception is documented. 8. Emergency Procurement Emergency procurement may be initiated when projected inventory is below the reorder point and the expected stockout occurs before the normal replenishment lead time. Emergency purchases require procurement approval. When possible, the procurement team should compare at least two available suppliers and document the reason for selecting the supplier. 9. Transportation and Logistics Transportation decisions should consider total transportation cost, delivery time, vehicle capacity, warehouse capacity, and customer demand. Optimization tools may be used to determine cost-efficient shipment allocations and routes while satisfying operational constraints. 10. Warehouse Capacity A proposed inbound shipment must not exceed the available storage capacity of the receiving warehouse. If the required quantity exceeds available capacity, the system should consider splitting the shipment or allocating inventory to another approved warehouse. 11. Critical Products Products classified as Critical must maintain a minimum service-level target of 95%. For critical products, stockout risk, supplier reliability, and lead time must be considered before reducing inventory or changing the supplier. 12. Purchase Order Approval Purchase orders above ₹500,000 require procurement manager approval. Purchase orders at or

Critical Products Products classified as Critical must maintain a minimum service-level target of 95%. For critical products, stockout risk, supplier reliability, and lead time must be considered before reducing inventory or changing the supplier. 12. Purchase Order Approval Purchase orders above ₹500,000 require procurement manager approval. Purchase orders at or below ₹500,000 may be approved by an authorized procurement officer, subject to budget availability and supplier compliance. 13. Data and Audit Requirements Procurement recommendations must be traceable to the data, calculations, policies, and constraints used to generate them. System-generated recommendations should record the relevant inventory values, demand forecast, supplier information, optimization result, and policy references where applicable. 14. AI Decision-Support Rules AI systems used for supply-chain decision support must not invent inventory quantities, supplier metrics, costs, lead times, or policy requirements. Numerical values must come from approved databases, machine-learning predictions, deterministic calculations, or optimization tools. Policy-related answers must be grounded in the latest approved policy documents. The AI system should clearly distinguish between calculated results, retrieved policy information, and recommendations. 15. Example Policy Scenario Example: Product P102 has current inventory of 200 units, a calculated reorder point of 350 units, and a forecasted demand of 500 units for the planning period. Because inventory is below the reorder point, replenishment should be evaluated. The final order quantity should consider EOQ, supplier capacity, lead time, warehouse capacity, and current risk conditions. 16. Policy Exceptions Any exception to this policy must be documented with the reason, affected product or supplier, approving authority, and date. Emergency exceptions should be reviewed after the event. 17. Review This policy shall be reviewed at least annually or when major changes occur in procurement processes, supplier contracts, inventory strategy, or regulatory requirements. End of Policy Document
